request.input:
Bill number: HB1032
<bill_text>
HOUSE BILL 1032

 By Dixie

 AN ACT to amend Chapter __ of the Public Acts of 2025
 (1st Ex. Sess. – SB 6002 / HB 6001); and
 Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 4; Title 5; Title
 6; Title 7; Title 8 and Title 49, relative to education.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 3, is amended by

adding the following as a new section:

 (a) As used in this section, "immigration officer" means any state, local, or

 federal law enforcement officer who is seeking to enforce immigration law, including, but

 not limited to, United States immigration and customs enforcement officers and United

 States customs and border protection officers.

 (b) Notwithstanding title 4, chapter 42 and title 7, chapter 68, the director of

 schools for the LEA or the director of the public charter school shall immediately notify all

 students enrolled in the LEA or public charter school, parents of students enrolled in the

 LEA or public charter school, and all educators, employees, and contractors of the LEA

 or public charter school of the presence of an immigration officer on the grounds of a

 public school controlled by the LEA or on the grounds of the public charter school.

 (c) Notwithstanding §§ 4-42-102 and 7-68-102, this section and any policy

 adopted by a local board of education or public charter school governing body to

 effectuate this section is not a sanctuary policy and does not subject a member of the

 local board or governing body, director of schools, director of the public charter school,

 or any employee of the LEA or public charter school to any penalty prescribed in title 4,

 chapter 42 or title 7, chapter 68 for the adoption or enforcement of a sanctuary policy.

 SECTION 2. This act takes effect upon becoming a law, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
This bill would require school directors for local education agencies (LEAs) and public charter schools to immediately notify all students, parents, educators, employees, and contractors if an immigration officer is on the school grounds. The bill defines an immigration officer as any state, local, or federal law enforcement officer seeking to enforce immigration law. It specifies that this notification requirement and any related policies are not considered sanctuary policies and do not subject school officials or employees to penalties associated with sanctuary policies. This act would take effect upon becoming law.
</summary>

assessments.summary_quote: The bill defines an immigration officer as any state, local, or federal law enforcement officer seeking to enforce immigration law.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the full operative definition. The named federal agencies are illustrative examples, not additional limits on its scope.

assessments.summary_quote: This bill would require school directors for local education agencies (LEAs) and public charter schools to immediately notify all students, parents, educators, employees, and contractors if an immigration officer is on the school grounds.
assessments.rationale: Identifies the responsible directors, immediate notification duty, all recipient groups, and school-grounds trigger. Omitting the statutory cross-references does not materially change the described duty.

assessments.summary_quote: It specifies that this notification requirement and any related policies are not considered sanctuary policies and do not subject school officials or employees to penalties associated with sanctuary policies.
assessments.rationale: Conveys both the non-sanctuary classification of the requirement and implementing policies and protection from sanctuary-policy penalties. 'School officials or employees' reasonably encompasses the listed board members, directors, and employees.
